Canada officially recognized a Palestinian state on 21 September 2025, marking a significant shift in its foreign policy. On 30 July 2025, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that Canada would officially recognize Palestine during the eightieth session of the United Nations General Assembly in September 2025 if certain conditions being met such as demilitarization, Hamas not being allowed to have a role, and presidential and legislative elections scheduled for 2026.

The announcement follows similar commitments from France and the U.K., marking a significant shift among Western powers traditionally cautious on Palestinian statehood. Canada joins more than 140 other members of the United Nations that have recognised a Palestinian state, in a break with long-standing policy despite strong opposition from Israel.
